messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the billing sync RFC — ran into a reconciliation gap yesterday when a batch request spanned two tenant routing keys. We emitted two partial charge events but the accounting job later collapsed them into one and lost the per-route attribution. Noticed undercount in tenant B.
kevin: ugh. do we have an example event payload?
maria: yes, pasted sanitized snippet: ```
{
  request_id: "r-9a3",
  tenant: "tenant-a",
  routes: ["model-x", "model-y"],
  tokens: {total: 1200, by_route: {"model-x": 800, "model-y": 400}}
} // then two charge events with same request_id but different route keys
```
jordan: is the accounting collapse keyed only by request_id? that feels brittle for multi-route.
maria: yep — current dedupe uses request_id as the canonical key to avoid double-charges from retries. but that loses resolution when we intentionally split billing by route.
kevin: options: 1) make dedupe key = request_id + route_id (simple) 2) keep request_id canonical but add attribution envelope with per-route deltas and change accounting to merge arrays 3) emit a parent event + child line-items so accounting always scans children
ejan: (typo: evan) i like 3 for auditability but it changes storage/modeling. can we handle it incrementally?
evan: +1 for parent/children. would let the reconciler detect missing children (audit) and still support single-event flows. tradeoff: heavier write amplification and more joins in the ledger.
maria: tradeoffs noted. also need to think about late-arrival corrections — we saw a late child arrive 7h later which triggered a partial refund but the refund logic only looks at fully finalized request_ids.
jordan: we should add a provenance pointer and finalized flag on each child: {parent_id, seq_no, provenance_ts, finalized_bool}. reconciler can have a finalized-only pass and an eventual-corrective pass.
kevin: how about a TTL window for correction claims? like 72h grace period where late arrivals cause automatic adjustments, afterwards they create an audit ticket rather than auto-adjust. keeps invoices stable.
evan: >72h seems reasonable for SEV-prone tenants, but we already have customers on Reserved who expect near-zero retrochanges. we might make TTL configurable per billing account.
maria: agreed — make claim-ttl configurable and surfaced in billing UI.
kevin: implementation notes: ingestion should attach a deterministic attribution_key = sha256(request_id + route_id + model_hash). accounting dedupe uses attribution_key first, falls back to request_id for legacy events.
jordan: also add an audit-marker event type when reconciler performs a merge/adjust. so audits can show human-readable diffs. include reason codes (LATE_ARRIVAL, DUPLICATE, MERGE).
evan: tests: unit for attribution_key collisions, e2e where child arrives after invoice generation, and sampling-based smoke for large batch jobs. backfill path: a canonicalizer service to convert legacy request_id-only events into parent/child shape with synthetic attribution_key and mark as legacy.
maria: summary action items: 1) ingestion: start emitting parent_id + child line-items + attribution_key (kevin) 2) accounting: support dedupe by attribution_key, fallback to request_id (jordan) 3) reconciler: two-pass finalized + corrective with configurable claim-ttl + emits audit-marker (evan) 4) backfill canonicalizer RFC (maria)
ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: metering-producer v2 -> canary tonight 02:30 UTC :rocket:
kevin: i'll start a PR for the ingestion schema change and include sample Avro. will link here when ready.
maria: thanks team. want to circle up tomorrow 10am to check PR and integration test plan. :thumbsup:
